Senses.Explanation: Literally “to bite and chew” (咬嚼), the term is attested 209 times in 109 allowlisted texts. Chan records extend the bodily action to sayings and public cases: one teacher tells beginners to “chew over a ready-made sentence that cannot be knocked down” and repeats “chew it over, chew it over” (咬嚼來、咬嚼去); the same record says Wujin spent his whole life unable to chew through “the bowl-carrying public case” (托缽公案). Other comments use the resistance of food as an explicit comparison: a saying can be “unable to be chewed through” (咬嚼不破), while Donglin offers only “wooden-slat soup and iron-nail rice—chew as you will” (木札羹、鉄釘飯，任汝咬嚼). The record also issues the opposite verdict, “strictly avoid chewing” (切忌咬嚼), after the answer “a thousand-year peach pit.”
Senses.Note: The Zen deviation is ordinary mastication used as a verb for sustained handling of a sentence, saying, or public case, with edible and inedible images kept visible. The corpus's affirmative instruction and prohibition are different appraisals of the same act, not separate senses. No independent high-value literal meal occurrence was found that would justify splitting actual eating from this lexicalized use.

Occurrences.Kwic: 且去咬嚼他一個顛撲不破的現成句子。咬嚼來、咬嚼去
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yunxi Langting Ting (雲溪俍亭挺禪師語錄): in his volume-four general address, Yunxi Langting Ting instructs beginning students to chew over an unbreakable ready-made sentence repeatedly until old masters' tongues can no longer deceive them.

Occurrences.Kwic: 只這秦時𨍏轢鑽，咬嚼不破。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yunxi Langting Ting (雲溪俍亭挺禪師語錄): Langting Jingting says that, without understanding, the Qin-era diamond drill is something one cannot chew through.

Occurrences.Kwic: 托缽公案，無盡一生咬嚼不破
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yunxi Langting Ting (雲溪俍亭挺禪師語錄): Langting Jingting answers an unnamed questioner that Wujin could not chew through the bowl-carrying public case for his entire life.

Occurrences.Kwic: 老宿曰：千年桃核。林泉道：切忌咬嚼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Empty Valley Collection (林泉老人評唱投子青和尚頌古空谷集): after the old monk's thousand-year peach pit, Linquan Conglun comments 'strictly avoid chewing.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 祇有木札羹、鉄釘飯，任汝咬嚼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)): in Kentang Yanchong's biography, Wanan Daoyan is the exact quoted teacher denoted by Donglin who tells his assembly that he has no special mystery, only wooden-slip soup and iron-nail rice for them to chew.
